answer: Each applicant registers a hilltop and a numbered kite with a crystal tail and flies it on 20 dawns in sixty days. Each morning, a neighbor photographs it and signs the log. From the valley, the warden reads the signal. Twice a season, the warden checks photos against wind records, and a fake kite fails the match. A forged log burns the 150 token bond, and the hilltop goes to the next in line. Faking ten thousand kites freezes 1,500,000 tokens, costs 600,000 dollars, and needs 200,000 flights. A kite that never leaves the ground is a toy. An identity that never flies at dawn stays one.
